mathematics.logical_review: Multiple independent AI-assisted readings verified the complete n3 numerical and structural route. The period-two base recognition proof was independently reconstructed using both a two-object Ore fraction category and explicit corner-fraction formulas. Checks covered derivation of the exact 1331 Koszul complexes from Hilbert/domain, exclusion of flattening ranks other than 33/22, the rank22 symmetric tensor normal form without external Kronecker classification, both support cases, rational-map degree multiplication, P1 pole-divisor growth, Frobenius duality and a length-three Koszul bimodule resolution for all unital modules. The conditional all-n AS-base theorem was independently audited and applied only after B-AS3 was proved. These checks are internal mathematical audits, not formal verification or external peer review.
mathematics.scope: Unconditional indexed two-step Ore exhaustion is now proved for n1,n2,n3 over the standing algebraically closed characteristic-zero field. For n3, all standard numerical data and period two lead to a pure-base AS3 recognition theorem, then to the general AS-base Ore theorem. Period one is established for the base B, not for final A. The all-n theorem still assumes B-ASn and finite resolutions; unconditional exhaustion and numerical automaticity for n>=4 remain open. No extra H/noetherian/Koszul/period hypotheses were silently inserted.

Opposite one-sided R_5 relations at distances 2 and 4 create forbidden cubic syzygies; distance 3 gives a verified monomial quotient with two prefix-distinct weight-42 code words and exponential row growth. No full exclusion of one-sided degeneration is asserted.
For n=1, the E^1/E^2 perfect pairing fixes top word length 3; domainness excludes weight-two and weight-six relations, so AS duality forces translation 6 and relation weights 3,4,5.

The two decompositions of the n=1 top Koszul tensor force both wx/xw coefficients nonzero; the exact resolution Euler recurrence yields the full standard Hilbert series, not only low-degree agreement.
General n=1 Ore compatibility is a_i c_i b_(i+2)=a_(i+3)b_i c_(i+1) and c_i d_(i+2)=a_(i+3)d_i. Normalization gives a=b=1, constant c and c d_(i+2)=d_i.

All residual word-linear basis changes preserve c and multiply the entire d sequence by one nonzero scalar. Augmentation-filtration linearization extends this existence criterion to bare indexed isomorphism.
The shift-one action is (alpha,beta)->(beta,c^(-1)alpha), giving alpha^2=c beta^2 as the exact period-one condition, including the zero pair. Shift two is always scalar-equivalent.
For the reverse construction, the sole PBW ambiguity, explicit differentials d1d2=d2d3=0 and both top tensor expansions were checked symbolically for both source parities with general parameters.
The w-count associated graded is the check algebra of k[x,z][w;tau], tau(x)=x, tau(z)=c z; it proves domainness and left/right noetherianity by leading terms and lifting finite generators.
Exact left and right Koszul resolutions and nondegenerate top pairings establish both AS conditions. The bimodule Koszul resolution bounds global dimension for all unital modules, not just simples.
The n=1 counterexample (c,alpha,beta)=(1,1,0) has alternating zz-projection ranks and cannot be check(D) for any single graded algebra D.
The excess-zero bar subcomplex is exactly the pure jump-one bar complex, with no new pure relations from positive excess.
For n3, D>=4 would give all pure-base simples projective dimension at most two; periodic row Hilbert ratios force an interior pole and exclude this.
In the pure-base numerical lemma, domain multiplication and the algebraically closed-field Segre dimension bound imply a common folded Hilbert pole of order at least two with leading coefficient cJ.
P(1)J=JP(1)=0 and JPprime(1)J=0 give r_i=2+q_i, q_i=q_(i+s-2), (s-2)sum q=L, leaving only s3 or s9.
The exceptional s9/L14 pattern folds to seven vertices and has determinant (1-u^7)^2(1-64u^7), contradicting polynomial growth at an interior positive root.
The mixed-rank row Hilbert limit gives a_i=b_(i+4), b_i=a_(i+5); period eight forces constancy. Positivity of the full inverse Hilbert polynomial forces a=b=3.
General AS-base Ore needs B itself ASn. AS pairings force D3 and r5=1, then multiplication by z dual forces r3=n, yielding a normal regular z family.
B has periods 2, L_B and L_B+5, so is period one without a commutativity assumption on periodicity maps.
The first Ore mapping cone is minimal without Koszulity. Low-excess bar components and full AS duality give all four Tor strands and the exact Hilbert product.

The weight-four relation projections are both isomorphisms by AS pairings; ordered spanning plus the exact Hilbert product proves PBW. Associativity and uniqueness prove indexed theta homomorphism and delta derivation identities.

The general R5 monomial quotient growth bound counts nonzero positions; using their sum as the count additionally uses the domain rank bound. The notes describe the exact limitation of that quotient test.

Quadratic standard Hilbert and domain give the exact left/right 1331 complexes: K3 has dimension one; its nonzero linear coefficient makes the top map injective; the remaining kernel has the same Hilbert series t^3 H. Koszulity is a conclusion of the period-two recognition theorem.

The two-period fold is an actual graded category using powers of one fixed periodicity isomorphism. Highest-degree terms preserve composable-domainness, and polynomial growth gives corner Ore fractions.
Faithful localization preserves all alternating product spaces X,Y. An independent corner realization x->xh(gh)^(-1), y->gy verifies the same multiplication and dimensions.

Domain relations contain no decomposable tensors. Segre dimension excludes flattening ranks 32/23; rank-one flattenings are also excluded. A rank22 tensor has full middle support and a rank-two defining hyperplane, yielding ua x+ub y+vb x+vc y.

For different supports U,W in a common three-dimensional X, the partial isomorphism has exactly the two cases determined by whether its common line is preserved. After framing, c q c^(-1)=lambda t or t^(-1).
The equalities dim XY=dim YX=6 force q=f(t) and c t c^(-1)=h(t) in k(t). f composed with h has degree one, so f is Möbius and dim XY<=5, contradiction.
For equal supports, conjugation by c is Möbius on k(t), and every alternating product has poles bounded by a divisor of degree O(m). This contradicts dim B_(0,2m)=binom(2m+2,2).

Nondegenerate top pairings identify dual right Koszul complexes with shifted left ones. The standard length-three Koszul bimodule resolution is split exact on each side and bounds global dimension for all unital modules.

N3-INDEXED-ORE uses numerical forcing, actual period two of B, the independent AS3 recognition theorem and the all-n conditional Ore theorem. B period one follows from periods two and AS translation three. Final A period one is not concluded.

For n3, delta(R) gives mu_i(id tensor L_(i+1))+(sigma_i sigma_(i+2))(L_i tensor id)=0. Nondegenerate top tensors imply full relation supports, so adjacent correction functionals vanish together. All-zero corrections give a normal w family and period three; periods two/three give final A period one. The all-nonzero branch is not settled.
